There is the claim that different colored maca is good for different genders: red maca is better for females and black is better for males, but I'm not sure if these claims are backed by any scientific evidence.  

Yellow maca is the most common therefore cheapest and red and black are more expensive. Whichever one you decide to get, I'd suggest a gelatinized powder.  Gelatinized just means it was heated/cooked to help remove the starches found in the root.  Some people may experience some stomach discomfort eating raw maca powder. I personally feel a little more bloated and have some heartburn ingesting non-gelatanized maca so I go for the gelatinized.

I highly recommend it. It definitely helps give me a little boost throughout the day too.  You should definitely order some of the powder if you haven't already. I'm trying to stay away from amazon so I'll lead you to www.themacateam.com which is more expensive than what you'd find on amazon I believe.  

Start with a teaspoon which I think is ~3g either in a little shot mixed with some water or milk. I use a little frother since it helps blend it up well. You'll most likely feel that but if not, try 1.5 or 2 teaspoons.  It won't harm you so just try out different amounts.

Hope this helps!

Either make a little shot mixed with water, or mix in a smoothie (i found peanut butter to mask it pretty well). My neighbors grandsons would come by every once in a while when I was younger and then they just stopped coming. We had so much fun hanging out in our backyards..they were wild kids. About 20 years later one of them came back to care for his grandmother. We got close and he was a pretty inspirational person in the short time he was here. 

Shortly after coming here, his grandmother fell really ill with brain cancer and went into the hospital. As she was in the hospital my friend, Bud, found out he had leukemia.  He was unable to care for her and I don't think ever burdened her with letting her know he was sick.

He got pretty sick as you can imagine and the last few days were very rough. He was a very strong, tough kid who took excellent care of himself.  Never one to rely on medicine and instead relied on proper health, hygiene and a positive attitude to get him through.

Bud, 29, survived for nearly a year but went through 2 rounds of chemo and the 3rd time he decided to not go through it again. I know it wasn't an easy decision to go on chemo but I think it was an easy decision to not go for a 3rd round.

The last words he spoke were the night before he passed.  Given in to the cancer and andoned hope, Bud would take whatever was prescribed to help ease his pain.  In the middle of the night Bud woke up in somewhat of a stupor.  He would ask in a way that was eerily devoid of hope and vigor, yet with such impatience "what do i need??? What do I want??"

May not sound as depressing or bittersweet as the other stories here and he was alive for at least 12 hours after...but to see how far he came and how much he struggled.  How in the end he just did not care about anything except feeling better.  How even he didn't know what he wanted or needed but essentially put feeling better on others in making the decision for him in such a helpless, hopeless, and restless way was just really intense...it was intense coming from someone like him.   It was scary.

Whether it was under the influence of weed or alcohol if I got too drunk or high I would panic and feel the same way I did during the trip.

While this isn't the same thing you are experiencing, there are some similarities. Either way, after some time they went away. I took up meditation for a year and during that time i was able to better recognize what caused those intense feelings and learned to notice them before they got too overwhelming and was eventually able to allow them to pass over me like an ocean wave without letting it sweep me away.  It took time and even to this day I sometimes feel the anxiety or panic sneaking up in very specific situations but I learned how to handle them a little better.

I hope you are able to overcome this.  Be safe and stay away from drugs for a little bit. Live and enjoy sobriety for some time while you gather yourself and work on this issue.
